proposedchanges.value: The Justice Department acknowledged removing website news releases about criminal cases arising from the January 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol. The department described the prosecution material as “partisan propaganda.” The releases had documented charges, convictions, and sentences connected with cases against people accused of taking part in the attack and trying to halt certification of the 2020 election. Removing those pages changed what readers could find through the department’s website, but it did not erase separate court records. The department’s characterization and the scope of the deletions drew attention because the releases documented federal prosecutions tied to an attack on Congress. The supplied reports describe the removal as part of a broader change in how the administration presented the event. They do not establish that court dockets or judicial records were deleted, or that the removed pages altered the outcomes of the cases. The episode concerns the department’s public archive and its description of the prosecutions.
